description: Structural-property primitives for the Run 35 value/plausibility scorer. A cross-domain transfer 'apply mechanism A to problem B' is PLAUSIBLE/VALUABLE when the structural properties A's mechanism REQUIRES (preconditions) are AFFORDED by problem B. Mechanism tokens are tagged with the properties they require; problem tokens with the properties they afford. value = coverage(preconditions by affordances).

properties.continuous: state/space is smooth and real-valued (not discrete)
properties.gradient_structure: there is a directional 'which way is better' signal
properties.objective_function: there is a scalar quantity to optimize or extremize
properties.stochastic: randomness / noise is intrinsic to the process
properties.population: many interacting units / a collection of candidates
properties.variation: units differ and the differences can be inherited/propagated
properties.competition: units compete for a limited shared resource
properties.conserved_quantity: some quantity is conserved and merely redistributed
properties.temporal_dynamics: the system evolves over time / has iteration
properties.feedback_loop: output feeds back to influence input
properties.equilibrium: the system settles toward a steady state
properties.threshold_effect: behavior changes abruptly past a critical point
properties.network_structure: entities and relations form a graph
properties.resource_constraint: a limited budget bounds what is possible
properties.measurable_state: the current state can be observed/quantified
properties.redundancy: replicated or repeated elements provide slack
properties.energy_landscape: there are basins/minima the system can fall into

tagging_rubric: Tag each token with the 2-4 properties most essential to it. For a MECHANISM token, tag what the mechanism REQUIRES of its substrate to work (e.g. 'gradient' requires continuous + gradient_structure + objective_function). For a PROBLEM token, tag what structure that problem AFFORDS / exhibits (e.g. 'allocation' affords discrete + resource_constraint + competition). Use ONLY these property names.
